# 1 Clement Chapter 48 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 48

---

## Council Notes

**On "mend" / "heal" / "repair" (v.1):** EMET: "heal." LOGOS: "mend." PNEUMA: "repair." The Greek *iasōmetha* (from *iaomai*) is a medical term: to heal. "Heal" (EMET) is most literal and carries the strongest therapeutic metaphor — the church has a wound requiring healing, not merely a structure requiring repair.

**On Psalm 118:19-20 citation (vv.2–3):** Clement quotes the LXX Psalm 117. The citation is accurate. All three agents render it with minor variations. LOGOS "give praise" vs. EMET "confess": the Greek *exomologēsomai* has both senses (confess, acknowledge, give thanks). "Confess" (EMET) is retained as theologically richer.

**On "gate of righteousness... in Christ" (v.4):** This is Clement's christological interpretation of Psalm 118 — the gate of righteousness is identified with Christ. All agents recognize this. LOGOS structures this as a relative clause ("the gate of blessedness — and all who..."); EMET gives a simpler reading. LOGOS preferred for clarity.

**On the virtue catalogue (vv.5–6):** Clement lists qualities: faithful (*pistos*), able to speak knowledge (*gnōsin*), wise in interpretation (*phronimos en diakrisei logōn*), pure in deeds. These appear to describe qualities of leadership. All agents translate reasonably. LOGOS "capable of declaring knowledge" is slightly awkward; EMET "able to speak forth knowledge" is retained.

**On "humble" / "humble-minded" (v.6):** LOGOS: "humble-minded." EMET: "humble." PNEUMA: "embrace humility." The Greek *tapeinophronein* is a compound: *tapeinōs* (low) + *phronein* (to think/mind). "Humble-minded" (LOGOS) best captures the Greek compound. Retained.

---

**48:1** Therefore let us quickly heal these divisions and fall down before the Master and beseech him with tears, that he may be merciful to us and be reconciled to us, and restore us to the honorable and pure conduct of brotherly love.

**48:2** For this is the gateway of righteousness opened unto life, as it is written: "Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter through them and confess the LORD.

**48:3** This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it."

**48:4** Therefore, while many gates stand open, this gate of righteousness that is in Christ is the gate of blessedness — and all who enter through it and direct their way in holiness and righteousness, performing all things without confusion, are blessed.

**48:5** Let a man be faithful; let him be able to speak forth knowledge; let him be wise in discernment of words; let him be pure in his actions —

**48:6** for the greater he seems to be, the more it befits him to be humble-minded, seeking the common benefit of all rather than his own.

---

*— SOPHIA*
